tasks.taskText: The CSS generator (lib/generator) automatically inserts a space between two adjacent tokens when leaving them adjacent would change how the text tokenizes (for example `1%` followed by `var(` or `#ff0000`). That rule is correct for values the parser turned into nodes, but it is also applied to Raw nodes, whose string value is re-tokenized on output. A raw value is text the parser deliberately left untouched (for example when parsing with `parseValue: false` or `parseRulePrelude: false`), so it must be emitted exactly as written. Today `generate(parse('span#foo { border: 1%var(--a)#ff0000; }', { parseRulePrelude: false, parseValue: false }))` returns `span #foo{border:1% var(--a) #ff0000}`; it must return `span#foo{border:1%var(--a)#ff0000}`. Automatic whitespace must still be inserted where a raw value meets its surroundings (the space in `@media screen` when the prelude is raw must stay) and for fully parsed values: `generate(parse('span#foo { border: 1%var(--a)#ff0000; }'))` must still give `span#foo{border:1% var(--a) #ff0000}`. The change belongs in lib/generator (create.js and its token-before logic). All existing generate, round-trip and source-map tests must keep passing; do not edit tests or fixtures.
